classification.difficultyReason: Convert the supplied diameter to radius, use the supplied total height to combine the cone volumes, and count only the two exposed curved surfaces using their supplied slant heights.

spec.description: Two cones joined at their common circular base; each slant height 15 cm, common diameter 18 cm and overall height 24 cm. Front common arc solid and rear arc dashed; no line joins the apexes.
spec.mathematics: r=9 cm, ℓ=15 cm for each cone, total perpendicular height 24 cm.

answer.worked:
The common radius is $18\div2=9$ cm. The cone heights add to $24$ cm.
$$\begin{align*}V&=\frac13\pi r^2(h_1+h_2)\\V&=\frac13\pi\times9^2\times24\\V&=648\pi\text{ cm}^3.\end{align*}$$

answer.short:
$270\pi\text{ cm}^2$

Only the two curved surfaces are exposed.
answer.worked:
The joined circular base is internal, so only the two curved surfaces contribute.
$$\begin{align*}S&=\pi r\ell+\pi r\ell\\S&=2\pi\times9\times15\\S&=270\pi\text{ cm}^2.\end{align*}$$
